title: Temporal signal profiles and assisted tooltip degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight design pattern we are calling 'Temporal Signal Profiles' to drive adaptive rendering and tooltip/legend behaviour in high-density time-series charts. The goal is to reduce CPU/GPU work and DOM churn for heavy queries while preserving clarity for keyboard and screen-reader users. This ticket covers design specs, token changes, and assisted tooltip degradation flows so engineering can implement a single, testable pattern across canvas and DOM render modes.
rationale: We observe two common failure modes: (1) interactive charts with long time ranges cause repeated reflow/paint and heavy event handling that degrades responsiveness; (2) accessible tooltip content and ARIA announcements are often verbosely synthesized for every hover/interact, causing noise and high-cost rendering on lower-end devices. Temporal Signal Profiles let the chart surface choose an appropriate fidelity and verbosity level based on user intent (hover vs. scrub vs. keyboard focus), point density, and performance budget.
proposed_solution: Add a small finite state model for chart interaction signals (Idle, Probe, Scrub, FocusedKeyboard) and attach a profile to each that controls: 1) tooltip rendering mode (full DOM, condensed DOM, aria-only announce), 2) legend updates frequency (throttled, batched, immediate), 3) visual fidelity hints (antialiasing on/off, simplify path sampling), and 4) tokenized UI labels (short vs. long form). Provide default profiles plus an API for engineers to override per-route. Update design tokens to include 'chart-tooltip-verbosity' and 'legend-update-window' and document semantic meanings.
decisions: Use a 4-state interaction model (Idle / Probe / Scrub / FocusedKeyboard) instead of continuous heuristics to make behaviour predictable for assistive tech.
Tooltips should surface condensed summaries by default in high-density views; expand to full detail on explicit keyboard open (Enter) or long press.
Implement ARIA announcements via a single aria-live region to avoid multiple simultaneous announcements and give a per-profile throttle.
Expose token names not values in the public token API (e.g., chart-tooltip-verbosity: 'condensed'|'detailed'|'announce-only') to avoid hard-coded pixel values in component code.
Fallback order: DOM tooltip -> canvas overlay -> aria-only depending on profile and device capability.
implementation_notes: Design tokens to add: chart-tooltip-verbosity, legend-update-window-ms, chart-simplify-threshold, tooltip-max-characters, aria-throttle-ms.
When point density > 2000 points in viewport, switch to 'condensed' profile automatically; density threshold configurable in runtime.
Canvas renderer should provide a lightweight hit-test layer to avoid expensive DOM event binding per data point.
Keyboard focus flow: single persistent tooltip component that reads concise summary and exposes 'details' button which then expands local DOM content (deferred hydration).
Mobile long-press opens detailed tooltip; short tap uses condensed inline peek to avoid full-screen overlay.
Provide feature-flag: temporal-profiles-enabled for gradual rollout and A/B measurements.
Add unit/e2e tests for aria-announcement throttling and legend update batching.
Coordinate with runtime team for perf targets: p99 interactive latency < 120ms on medium-sized charts (as measured on internal perf harness).
Opt for incremental rollout to Dedicated customers via config, default enabled for Hosted new versions.
Document degradation stories for air-gapped/private installations where JS might be older: fall back to safe condensed profile.
Design the condensed tooltip copy using existing microcopy tokens to keep translations minimal (use token chart-tooltip-condensed-template).
Avoid embedding large DOM trees per point; use a single DOM shell reused across interactions.
Accessibility note: screen-reader users should be able to disable announcement throttling via user settings; surface this as a per-user preference in our accessibility settings.
Prototyping in Figma should include three density variants: sparse (<=200 points), medium (200-2000), dense (>2000) with interaction flows.
Include visual regression snapshots for condensed vs expanded tooltip states in Percy/GH checks.
Add a lightweight telemetry event: chart-tooltip-mode-changed and chart-legend-update-batched to tie to cost dashboards.
Engineering should avoid using innerText continuously; prefer prebuilt tokenized strings with placeholders to reduce GC pressure.
For RTL support ensure token templates place numeric values at the end to avoid bidi confusion.
Coordinate with localization for shortened forms; provide map file for long -> short translations.
Keep API surface minimal: ChartConfig.temporalProfile?: 'auto'|'condensed'|'detailed'|'announce-only'.

review_feedback: PM (Lina Park): please add acceptance criteria that include telemetry events and a rollback path if we see accessibility regressions.
Engineering (Ravi Singh): prefer exposing numeric thresholds via config, not baked tokens; keep tokens for semantics only.
Accessibility (Jamal Ortiz): ensure condensed tooltip still exposes numeric values clearly and that screen-reader flow reads only once per focus.
DesignOps (Aisha Gomez): add translations map for condensed copy to reduce translator overhead; include character limits in token definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Default 'auto' profile picks condensed mode for dense views and preserves full detail for sparse views (validated by unit tests).
ARIA announcements are throttled and do not exceed one announcement per 400ms by default; configurable via token.
Tooltip DOM component is reused (single shell) to avoid per-point DOM churn (verified with DOM snapshot tests).
Percy snapshots show no visual regressions across dense/medium/sparse prototypes.
Telemetry events emitted: chart-tooltip-mode-changed and chart-legend-update-batched.
Perf target: p95 interactive latency improves or remains within 10% of baseline for medium charts; p99 < 120ms goal.
Localization mapping for condensed tooltip is provided and approved by Localization team.
Docs: Figma spec and Confluence design doc linked and updated with tokens table.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Condensed tooltips may omit critical context for screen-reader users. Mitigation: Provide explicit 'Details' action to expand the tooltip and expose full DOM content.

Risk: Automatic switching may confuse users when fidelity changes mid-interaction. Mitigation: Use clear animation and a short toast for first-time exposure to explain behavior (opt-out via settings).
Risk: Token naming inconsistency. Mitigation: Add a migration guide in tokens repo and a short deprecation window for old token names.
Risk: Performance work spills into runtime coupling. Mitigation: Keep profile semantics declarative and let runtime team implement optimizations behind a feature flag.
